items.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He wrote a book with John Benitez on Latino bass playing. So he’s very knowledgeable, so he plays with the band periodically.

ctx.x: Because the first time I tried to at least absorb some of this Latin music and much of it where the bass is anticipating, and it just seemed so incorrect. We’re used to jazz, we’re used to walking bass, we’re hitting the downbeats, even if it’s a funky thing usually.

Well it happened yesterday, the young man caught on very quickly, but I had to tell him [scats] and then he went down to [scats] which is good too, that’s an older style as I mentioned to him. And that worked out very nicely what he was doing. But yes you have to be very knowledgeable. I have a bass player that played with Tito Puente for many years and he played with Rubén Blades, I don’t know if you know that particular name. But he’s very experienced in the field for the past fifteen years or so. And then the…

not necessarily the same thing so how do you do it without getting in the way. So that’s one thing that I haven’t looked into you know, that much. I depend on them to sort of do it, if I happen to use a guitar player.
